learning_outcomes.text: Students can justify and explain the necessities and importance of IT systems, programming, and data science in mechanical engineering, and how these tools can solve practical challenges in mechanical engineering.

Students have a basic understanding of computers and can use relevant operating system functions. They have sufficient knowledge of the Python programming language to understand and execute Python programs, and to independently solve simple problems relevant to mechanical engineering by programming.

Technical concepts such as data types and data structures, as well as procedural implementation and object orientation, are known. Furthermore, theoretical and practical basic knowledge of algorithms in general, as well as data analysis and data evaluation, is available.

Students know the importance of data formats, data models, and communication protocols for network communication. They are familiar with various hardware and software architectures. Furthermore, they have acquired a basic understanding of data transmission between software and hardware components and have reinforced this through practical experience.

This establishes relevant IT fundamentals for further study in mechanical engineering, and students are particularly able to use Python with external libraries (e.g., sympy) to solve problems in other (compulsory) courses such as HM and TM.

syllabus_topics: Programming environment Jupyter Notebook/Anaconda for Python
Python libraries for Mechanical Engineering and Data Science
Fundamentals/application of Data Science in Mechanical Engineering
Programming tasks individually and in groups
assessment_rules: The module grade is determined by the grade of the written examination.
